rationale: Fire damage to the policyholder's own kitchen cabinets, ceiling, and walls from an accidental grease flare-up on their stove is clearly direct property damage to the home's structure and contents.
claim_summary: Kitchen fire caused by grease flare-up on stove yesterday evening. Charred cabinets above stove and smoke damage to ceiling and walls. No injuries; fire was contained using extinguisher. Damage estimated in the $2,000–$25,000 range. Policy POL-1001 is active with $500 deductible and adequate coverage.

case_facts.incident_type: kitchen fire from grease flare-up on stove
case_facts.damage_description: charred kitchen cabinets above stove, smoke damage on ceiling and walls
case_facts.scope_of_damage: confined to kitchen area, rest of house unaffected

rationale: Water damage to the policyholder's own residential structure (hardwood floor, drywall) and contents (stored boxes) caused by failure of the policyholder's internal plumbing system is a classic property damage claim.
claim_summary: Sam Patel (POL-1004) reports a basement flood caused by a burst supply line under the upstairs bathroom sink that ran for approximately two days while claimant was away. Damage includes approximately 2 inches of standing water, buckled hardwood floors, drywall soaked to 1 foot, and multiple ruined stored boxes. Estimated damage likely exceeds $25,000.

case_facts.damage_description: hardwood floor buckled, drywall soaked to about one foot, stored boxes ruined
case_facts.water_source: burst supply line under upstairs bathroom sink, ran for approximately two days

rationale: Wind damage to the policyholder's own roof structure (four shingles on back porch overhang) is straightforward property damage coverage.
claim_summary: Policyholder Jordan Lee (POL-1006) reports wind damage to back porch roof overhang: four shingles blown off, estimated repair cost $400, no water intrusion or secondary damage. Low-severity claim eligible for standard property damage handling.
